meta.title: Add tail call optimization to VM
meta.body_summary: Add tail call optimization to VM by implementing TCO for OpCall, OpCall2, and OpCallV and including a tail-recursive factorial test.

perf_labels.notes: Single-commit TCO with test, no review or discussion; closed by author within 30 seconds, likely not a mergeable PR.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 77 changed lines, this is a small edit by absolute volume. It adds TCO as a single commit with 77 additions across 4 files. As a new feature optimization PR, it was closed immediately by the author, which is inconsistent with a typical merge workflow. The small scope suggests it could have been a mergeable performance improvement if it were correct and properly reviewed.

review_details.performance_claim: Implement tail call optimization for OpCall, OpCall2, OpCallV to improve performance of recursive functions.
review_details.rejection_signals: Author closed PR within 30 seconds of creation, with no review engagement. No explicit rejection signals available.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: The PR was closed by the author without any maintainer interaction, so no capability boundary was tested. The edit itself (TCO in VM) is a complex optimization, but the outcome does not reflect technical inadequacy, rather a process outcome.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: Only a tail-recursive factorial test added; no performance benchmarks or profiler evidence.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: No merge, so no regression handling.

core_change_summary.description: In runtime/vm/vm.go, added tail call optimization for OpCall, OpCall2, and OpCallV by reusing the current frame when the call is in tail position. Added tail-recursive factorial test in tests/vm/valid/ as a .mochi file with expected output.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Expected output files represent the post-optimization expected results.
change_trajectory: Single commit adding TCO to VM and a validation test.

collaboration_trajectory: PR opened with TCO implementation and closed by author 27 seconds later with no review or comment activity.
